en.title: Minimum Increment Added to Non-Adjacent Positions
en.description:
Choose any set of pairwise non-adjacent positions and add the same non-negative integer x to all of them, in this single operation only, so that the array becomes non-decreasing. Find the minimum x; output -1 if it is impossible. If the array is already non-decreasing, you may choose the empty set and take 0.

The standard input/output format and examples were compiled by this site; ranges explicitly marked as this site's are not the source's original constraints.
en.input: The first line contains n, and the second line contains the array. The source gives no numeric bounds; on this site 1≤n≤200000, −10^9≤element≤10^9.
hints: Each descent in the original array forces its right end to be chosen and its left end not to be chosen; if two forced positions are adjacent, there is immediately no solution. Take the maximum descent amount as x, add x only to the forced positions, then verify the whole array.
